details:
=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- docs/INVENTORY.md:268-272 | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [openai_gpt-6-luna]
  PROBLEM: The Scripts inventory omits the new `scripts/provider_outage.py`.
  WHY: `tests/inventory_parity.py` compares tracked scripts with the inventory, so the Inventory parity CI step fails.
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml:5052-5078 | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_8-flash, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: The empty-noop branch extracts only `marker=` from the failure fingerprint and does not export provider-outage state to `$GITHUB_ENV`.
  WHY: During a provider outage, downstream steps can post misleading retry guidance, apply `ai:review-blocked`, or send a per-PR alert instead of taking the paused-provider path.
- scripts/provider_outage.py:725-728 | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_8-flash, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: `_resume` closes every outage marker even when recovery operations recorded errors or an opt-in release rerun failed.
  WHY: Once the marker is closed, later ticks cannot retry failed dispatches or cleanup, leaving affected PRs or repositories stranded.
- scripts/provider_outage.py:696 | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_8-flash, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: Recovery uses the outage marker issue’s creation time as `window_start` while filtering candidate PRs by `updated_at`.
  WHY: The triggering PR can have been updated before the marker was created and is then skipped during recovery; severity disagreement: one reviewer rated this major, while the others rated it blocker.
- scripts/provider_outage.py:624 | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_8-flash, minimax_minimax-m3, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: The hold-release check treats a PR as conflicted only when `mergeable_state == "dirty"`.
  WHY: Other unmergeable or unconfirmed states can be treated as conflict-free, allowing an outage hold to be released and a review claim posted.
- scripts/provider_outage.py:272-273 | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_8-flash, minimax_minimax-m3, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: `latest_review_outcome` accepts an editor-summary comment without checking whether it belongs to the current head SHA.
  WHY: A summary for another head can override a current-head `provider_unavailable` failure, causing the PR to be skipped during recovery.
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py:1398-1427 | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_8-flash, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: Reviewer logs and `status_*.txt` files share one alphabetically sorted list and the same 32 MiB total read budget.
  WHY: Large logs can exhaust the budget before success status files are read, causing a partial reviewer failure to be misclassified as a provider-wide outage.
- scripts/provider_outage.py:525-563 | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_8-flash, minimax_minimax-m3, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: Concurrent `record` calls can each create a marker and see only their own issue in the post-create listing.
  WHY: Both calls can report `action=created` with `alert=True`, producing duplicate open markers and operator alerts.
- .github/workflows/review_autofix_sweep.yml:109-144 | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_8-flash, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: The `provider-outage-probe` job does not honor `inputs.dry_run` on manual workflow dispatch.
  WHY: A manual dry run can still perform recovery side effects, including dispatching reviews, removing labels, releasing holds, rerunning a release, and closing the marker; severity disagreement: one reviewer rated this nit, while the others rated it major.
- .github/workflows/review_autofix_sweep.yml:103-167 | severity=high | confidence=[3]
  flagged_by: [qwen_qwen3_7-plus]
  PROBLEM: The `provider-outage-probe` job has no `concurrency:` group to prevent overlapping probe and resume executions.
  WHY: Overlapping ticks can duplicate resume comments, review dispatches, label removal, hold releases, and recovery alerts.
- scripts/provider_outage.py:664-689 | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: A probe that cannot succeed has no max-age or bailout path for its open outage marker.
  WHY: A misconfigured probe model or missing API key can leave review dispatches paused indefinitely without alerting an operator.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===
- requirement: Every new tracked script in `scripts/` must be listed in `docs/INVENTORY.md` under the Scripts section.
  expected_change_site: `docs/INVENTORY.md`, `## Scripts` section
  confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_8-flash, minimax_minimax-m3, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  EVIDENCE: `scripts/provider_outage.py` is absent from the PR’s inventory changes; the inventory parity test reports it missing.
- requirement: The plan at `docs/plans/issue-5773-provider-outage-wait-and-resume-plan.md:87` specifies CLI subcommands `record`, `status`, `tick` for `scripts/provider_outage.py`.
  expected_change_site: `scripts/provider_outage.py`, `build_parser()`
  confidence=[3]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_8-flash, minimax_minimax-m3, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  EVIDENCE: `build_parser()` registers `record` and `tick`, but does not register `status`.
- requirement: The empty-noop branch must export `AUTOFIX_PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE=true` and `AUTOFIX_PROVIDER_OUTAGE` when the reason is `provider_unavailable`.
  expected_change_site: `.github/workflows/review_autofix.yml`, “Post editor summary comment” step, empty-noop branch
  confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  EVIDENCE: The branch extracts only `marker=` and does not parse `reason=` or `provider_outage=` or write the provider flags to `$GITHUB_ENV`.
- requirement: “It posts an ‘AI review/autofix paused: model provider unavailable’ comment.”
  expected_change_site: `.github/workflows/review_autofix.yml`, empty-noop branch of “Post editor summary comment”
  confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [openai_gpt-6-luna]
  EVIDENCE: The branch builds the generic retry comment and sets `AUTOFIX_EDITOR_EMPTY_NOOP=true`, which excludes the later provider-paused comment step.
=== END CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- scripts/provider_outage.py:725-728 | severity=critical | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: `_resume` closes every outage marker unconditionally, even when `summary["errors"]` is non-empty.
  WHY: Failed resume work cannot be retried after the marker closes, leaving affected PRs or repositories stranded.
- scripts/provider_outage.py:696 | severity=critical | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: `_resume` derives `window_start` from the marker issue’s `created_at`, then `resume_repo` skips PRs updated before that time.
  WHY: The triggering PR can have an `updated_at` earlier than the marker creation time and be permanently skipped during recovery.
- scripts/provider_outage.py:272-273 | severity=high | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: `latest_review_outcome` accepts an editor-summary comment without verifying that it belongs to the current head SHA.
  WHY: A later summary can override a current-head `provider_unavailable` failure, preventing the PR from being considered a resume candidate.
- scripts/provider_outage.py:624 | severity=high | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The hold-release check identifies conflicts only when `mergeable_state == "dirty"`.
  WHY: A PR in another unmergeable state can be treated as conflict-free and have its outage hold released.
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py:1398-1427 | severity=high | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: Reviewer logs and status files share one alphabetical ordering and 32 MiB total read budget.
  WHY: Large logs can exhaust the budget before successful reviewer status files are read, leading to false provider-wide outage classification.
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml:5052-5078 | severity=high | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The empty-noop branch extracts only `marker=` and posts a generic retry message without exporting provider-outage state.
  WHY: A provider outage can receive misleading retry guidance instead of the paused-provider message.
- scripts/provider_outage.py:525-563 | severity=high | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: Concurrent `record` calls can each create an issue and see only their own issue in the re-list.
  WHY: Both can alert and leave duplicate open outage markers.
- .github/workflows/review_autofix_sweep.yml:109-110 | severity=low | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The `provider-outage-probe` job does not check `inputs.dry_run`.
  WHY: A manual dry run can still execute live recovery side effects.
- Requirement: "Every new tracked script in `scripts/` must be listed in `docs/INVENTORY.md` under the Scripts section" — repository convention enforced by `tests/inventory_parity.py:253-269`, run in `.github/workflows/ci.yml:1087-1090`. The implement-plan lesson from PR #5864 explicitly states "a new `scripts/` file needs its `docs/INVENTORY.md` entry in the same PR."
  Expected change site: `docs/INVENTORY.md`, `## Scripts` section, alphabetically near `scripts/workflow_failure_heal_autofix_report.sh`
  Evidence of absence: `docs/INVENTORY.md` is not in `pr_changed_files.txt`. No diff hunk adds `scripts/provider_outage.py` to the inventory. `tests/inventory_parity.py` will report `missing scripts/provider_outage.py` and CI will fail on the final merge PR.
  SEVERITY: BLOCKER
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
- Requirement: "The plan at `docs/plans/issue-5773-provider-outage-wait-and-resume-plan.md:87` specifies CLI `record`, `status`, `tick`." The shipped `build_parser()` registers `record` and `tick` only.
  Expected change site: `scripts/provider_outage.py`, `build_parser()` (around line 788)
  Evidence of absence: `sub.add_parser("status", ...)` is absent. Only `record` and `tick` are registered. The plan's enumerated list is unambiguous. If `status` was intentionally dropped because the `tick` JSON output serves the same purpose, the plan text and the PR description checklist should note the deviation but do not.
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 3
=== END FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
